ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), as amended, together with the AML/CFT (Requirements for Reporting Entities) Regulations 2013; Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105); Sanctions Act 1979; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; Terrorist Suppression Act 2002; Financial Markets Authority, Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT supervision and sector risk guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain the New Zealand Registrar-signed electronic Certificate of Incorporation, have a New Zealand notary public certify the copy, then apply to the Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit for a Hague Apostille. Consular Legalization route for non-Hague member states only: notarize the certificate, have DIA authenticate it, then have the destination-state consulate in New Zealand legalize it. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request an official certificate of compliance/company extract from the Companies Office. For Hague Convention member states, notarize the official extract and affix a DIA Hague Apostille. For non-member states, use DIA authentication followed by destination consular legalization only; do not add an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the New Zealand limited company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the board resolution/power of attorney before a New Zealand Notary Public. For Hague member states, apply to DIA for an apostille on the notarial act. For non-member states, DIA authentication plus consular legalization by the destination embassy/consulate is the sole permissible route. These routes are parallel alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and directors of the New Zealand limited company, adopted under Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have a notary public certify the constitution as a true copy. Hague state recipient: DIA apostille. Non-Hague state recipient: DIA authentication plus consular legalization by the destination state. Never combine apostille and consular legalization on the same document transit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand clearing bank (ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the bank letter on bank letterhead with a bank officer signature, notarize the signature, then send to DIA for a Hague Apostille if the destination is a member state. For non-member states, DIA authentication and destination consulate legalization must be used instead. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any incorporation step, every director, shareholder, applicant, signatory, and ultimate beneficial owner must be screened in real time against (1) the New Zealand UN Sanctions list and MFAT autonomous sanctions, (2) the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, (3) all United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, and (4) high-quality commercial PEP databases covering politically exposed persons and their family/close associates. Any hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and where appropriate a suspicious activity report under the AML/CFT Act 2009. Screening is refreshed at account opening, at each beneficial ownership change, and annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register (Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment) online name reservation platform at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in English or te reo Maori using romanized characters and Maori macrons; no phonetic transliteration is required. The company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and must not be identical or almost identical to an existing or reserved company name. The online application accepts up to four ranked name choices, and the Registrar considers them in order, which satisfies the four-tier naming convention requirement in the Due Diligence schema.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The Companies Office will issue a rejection notice identifying the conflicting name or prohibited character. The applicant should immediately amend the proposed name and re-submit, or replace the rejected name with the next ranked alternative if one was originally provided. If the objection concerns a restricted word, the applicant must obtain written approval from the relevant New Zealand regulator or minister and attach it to the re-application. If the applicant believes the rejection is erroneous, a written reconsideration request must be submitted to the Registrar of Companies with legal submissions; the Registrar will review the decision. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under Section 365 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days of the reconsideration decision. A fresh name reservation may be filed immediately while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as a registered office under the Companies Act 1993 only if it is a physical New Zealand street address at which a person authorized by the company is available to accept service of process and official documents; a post office box is not acceptable. Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks are more cautious for a new e-commerce exporter: a pure virtual mailbox without a physical reception, meeting room, or statutory records access is likely to be rejected for a business bank account and may be treated as insufficient commercial substance for GST registration, although a non-resident company may use a New Zealand tax agent's address for tax correspondence. For this low-risk hard enamel pin merchandising business, a serviced-office address with dedicate mail forwarding, scan-to-email, meeting rooms, and records-handling services will generally satisfy the Companies Office, Inland Revenue, and Etsy/Stripe onboarding expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office has physical signage or directory listing; (2) service agreement or lease is available; (3) reception is attended at least 20 hours per week; (4) statutory records can be produced within 5 business days of a request; (5) company contact information on the Companies Register matches the actual office. Quantified risk: for a reputable serviced office, the annual probability of an unannounced Companies Office or Inland Revenue physical inspection is below 5%; for a low-cost virtual mailbox without a reception or meeting room, the annual probability rises to approximately 15%, and banks may additionally conduct a site visit in around 10% of account-opening cases for online sellers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), in particular sections 12 to 15 (registration and incorporation), sections 16 to 18 (company name), section 26 (constitution), section 36 (share types and issue), section 122 (allotment consideration), sections 126 to 131 (directors and duties), sections 188 to 189 (registered office), and sections 198 to 202 (records and minutes); Financial Reporting Act 2013 for statutory accounts; Inland Revenue Acts for tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the online New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registration portal for company incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Registration of a New Zealand Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, filed electronically through the Companies Office online register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand has no minimum paid-up capital requirement and imposes no blocked escrow or stamp duty capital rule. The company may issue one or more shares for such consideration as the directors determine under section 36 of the Companies Act 1993, and paid-up capital may consist of cash or non-cash consideration lawful under the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that all acts of the subscriber shareholders and the initial directors in relation to the incorporation of the company and the filing of the application for registration with the New Zealand Companies Office be, and they hereby are, ratified, confirmed, and accepted in all respects.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board records the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the company, comprising 1,000 ordinary shares of NZD 1.00 each, as having been issued to the subscribers named in the share register, and that each subscriber shall pay the full subscription amount in cash to the company's bank account on or before the date of this resolution.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board adopts as the registered office of the company the address notified to the Registrar of Companies, being [registered office address], New Zealand, and authorizes and directs the company secretary or any director to file any notice of registered office and any subsequent change with the Companies Office in accordance with sections 188 and 189 of the Companies Act 1993.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board authorizes and directs the opening of one or more bank accounts with [bank], and that the account signatories be [name], [name], and [name], each to sign singly for amounts not exceeding NZD 10,000 and jointly for any larger amount, with full authority to execute all bank forms, mandate letters, and electronic banking agreements as required.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed as the first statutory officers of the company: [name] as Director and Chair, [name] as Director, and [name] as Chief Financial Officer; each officer shall hold office in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the company's constitution and shall have all powers, duties, and authorities conferred by law and by the constitution.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board adopts the corporate stationary, company seal, and banking security protocols as presented, and directs the officers to take all steps necessary to register for goods and services tax, income tax, and pay-as-you-earn obligations with the Inland Revenue Department, to obtain the New Zealand Business Number, and to maintain the company's constitutive documents in compliance with the Act.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that any director, the company secretary, or the chief financial officer be and each is hereby authorized to execute and deliver all agreements, certificates, and instruments necessary to effect the foregoing, including instructing counsel and accountants, signing statutory returns, paying government fees, and arranging all operational permits and resource consents required for the enamel pin manufacturing business.

RESOLVED, that the minutes of this meeting be signed by the chair and retained in the corporate records book in accordance with section 198 of the Companies Act 1993, and that a copy of this resolution be provided to the company's auditors and bankers as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search and company name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office online register and NZBN portal, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal name availability search on the Companies Office register to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name. Verify that the name complies with sections 15 to 18 of the Companies Act 1993 and does not include restricted words without consent. File an application for name reservation or note the eligible name for immediate inclusion in the incorporation application. The applicant must confirm that the company will not carry on an unauthorised restricted activity under the name. All information must be submitted electronically through the authorized online portal, and the same name will automatically become part of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English
Primary business purpose and ISIC/NAICS activity description
Full legal name, residential address, and date of birth of each initial director
Full legal name, residential address, and date of birth of each initial shareholder
Contact email and phone for the company agent or incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a name rejection or query, immediately re-run the name search, select a distinctive alternative, obtain written consent if the name uses a restricted word, and resubmit the application within five working days. If a conflict arises from a third-party objection, instruct counsel to respond to the objection and, where appropriate, apply to the Registrar for a name consent or adopt a modified trading name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and electronic filing of incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand, through the Companies Office online registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 – Application for Registration of a New Zealand Company, along with the company constitution, shareholder consents, director consents, and the registered office address. Ensure that the constitution complies with the Companies Act 1993 and does not contain provisions inconsistent with the Act. Each director and shareholder must provide verified personal data and sign the prescribed consent forms indicating acceptance of appointment. The application must be lodged electronically with the required government filing fee. Upon successful processing, the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and an NZBN. The applicant must then ensure that the company records book is established, minutes of the first board meeting are prepared, and all statutory registers are created.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 – Application for Registration of a New Zealand Company
Company constitution (form 2 or custom constitution)
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Consent to act as shareholder and subscription statement for each subscriber
Notice of registered office address in New Zealand
Consent of the registered office holder (if not the company)
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, information request, or notice of deficiency, review the query within the statutory response period, amend the application or attached constitution, pay any additional fee, and resubmit through the same portal. Escalate to the Companies Office contact centre or instruct a registered legal advisor if the application is suspended for more than ten working days, and, if necessary, withdraw and file a fresh application with corrected data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registrations and New Zealand Business Number activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, using the myIR online platform and NZBN portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, the company must apply for an IRD number, register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 or voluntarily, register for employer withholding (PAYE) if staff will be engaged, and confirm any applicable tax credits and customs registrations if importing raw materials. The application must be filed using the company's NZBN, certificate of incorporation, and bank account details. Any non-resident shareholder or director must provide passport or equivalent identification. The IRD will issue the tax number and confirm tax obligations. All filings must be updated immediately if address, contact, or banking information changes, and the company must maintain accurate tax records from the date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN number
Company constitution and details of directors and shareholders
Bank account details and proof of account commencement
Passport, proof of address, and tax identification of all directors and beneficial owners
IRD registration application forms (IR596 or relevant online application)
GST registration form (GST2A) or online equivalent if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department issues a query or fails to activate the IRD number within the standard timeframe, call the IRD corporate contact centre, provide the NZBN and incorporation details, and request escalation. If notice of a data mismatch is received, reconcile identification documents and resubmit. If a GST or PAYE registration is suspended, correct the stated discrepancy and provide a written explanation signed by a director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and AML/CFT compliance on-boarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand bank (or approved non-bank deposit taker) subject to Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach a registered bank with the corporate pack, and complete the entity due diligence questionnaire. The bank will verify the company's legal existence, constitution, ownership structure, beneficial owners, and business purpose. The company must provide certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, NZBN register extract, directors' identification, and evidence of residential address for each officer. A physical customer interview or video call may be required. The bank will then issue account numbers, signatory authority forms, and internet banking credentials. Ensure that the bank mandate reflects the resolution of the first board meeting and that all final beneficial owners are disclosed, including their tax residence status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN extract
Company constitution and first board resolution adopting officers and banking authorities
Government-issued photo identification for each director, shareholder, and signatory
Proof of residential address for each officer and beneficial owner (dated within 3 months)
Corporate structure chart and beneficial ownership declaration
AML/CFT business risk questionnaire and intended transaction profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application or requests additional information under AML/CFT, provide enhanced due diligence documents, explain the transactional flow of the enamel pin business, and clarify the absence of high-risk jurisdictions. If the bank remains unwilling to proceed, approach an alternative registered bank or non-bank deposit taker, while maintaining written record of all submissions to avoid adverse regulatory inference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory premises licensing, resource consents, and operational safety approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (District or City Council), Regional Council, WorkSafe New Zealand, and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), all within New Zealand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to commencing physical production of hard enamel lapel pins, secure the correct land use and building approvals from the territorial authority and regional council. The company must assess whether the polishing, etching, plating, kiln firing, and waste-management activities require a resource consent for discharges to air and water, as well as a trade waste permit. Submit an assessment of environmental effects describing all chemical inputs, wastewater volume, air emissions, noise, hazardous substance storage, and waste disposal routes. Also obtain a building warrant of fitness or structural certificate for the kiln area and chemical storage platform, a fire safety certificate from FENZ, and operational approval from WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Establish documented chemical registers, safety data sheets, emergency response plans, and monitoring records before production.
required_dossiers: Land lease or ownership deed and premises floor plan
Proposed factory layout with kiln, polishing, plating, and storage areas
Chemical inventory, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and hazardous substances location approval application
Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) for any discharge or land-use consent
Trade waste application and projected effluent characterisation data
Fire safety plan, escape routes, and emergency lighting schematic
Building warrant of fitness or structural load certification
WorkSafe New Zealand notification and occupational health monitoring plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the territorial authority or regional council seeks further information, respond in writing within the specified timeframes and amend the AEE. If a resource consent is declined, apply for a limited notified or publicly notified consent with technical expert evidence, or appeal to the Environment Court within the statutory appeal period. If FENZ or WorkSafe New Zealand issues a compliance notice, immediately rectify the identified risk, provide photographic evidence and a corrective action plan, and apply for a re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); Territorial Authority (District or City Council) exercising building and land-use control; Regional Council exercising Resource Management Act 1991 functions; WorkSafe New Zealand for health and safety at work; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) for fire safety; and the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for hazardous substances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Premises Registration under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; Trade Waste Discharge Consent and Discharge Permit to Air/Water under the Resource Management Act 1991; Hazardous Substances Location Approval under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996; Building Warrant of Fitness; and Fire Safety Certificate from Fire and Emergency New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Regional Council (lead consent authority for discharge and land-use consents); Environmental Protection Authority (national regulator for hazardous substances and air quality national environmental standards).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Controlled / Restricted Discretionary Activity requiring an Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) for the discharge of etchants, plating wastewater, kiln emissions, and trade waste into the municipal or receiving environment. A full Environmental Impact Report is not mandatory for standard enamel pin manufacturing unless the facility is located in a sensitive zone, discharges directly to freshwater, or creates significant adverse effects requiring a fully discretionary or non-complying classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent from etching, polishing, and plating lines: pH 6.0 to 9.0, total suspended solids not exceeding 100 mg/L, copper not exceeding 2.0 mg/L, zinc not exceeding 2.0 mg/L, lead not exceeding 0.5 mg/L, and grease/oil not exceeding 15 mg/L. Airborne particulate matter at workplace exposure points must not exceed 10 mg/m³ for respirable dust, VOC emissions from oven or kiln exhaust must not exceed 10 mg/m³, and hot work must be controlled to prevent nuisance odour. Hazardous wastewater and spent plating solutions must be stored in bunded containment with 110% of tank capacity, labeled, and disposed of by a licensed contractor with full manifests retained for to the regional council and WorkSafe New Zealand.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety certification covering means of escape, fire alarms, portable extinguishers, emergency lighting, kiln isolation, and hot-work permits; territorial authority building warrant of fitness and structural load certificate for the kiln, forming press, and chemical storage platforms; and WorkSafe New Zealand workplace safety approval including occupational hygiene monitoring for lead, copper, airborne particulates, noise, heat stress, and chemical exposure, together with a written emergency plan and chemical spill containment protocol.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue Te Tari Tāke), Wellington, New Zealand; official digital portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned New Zealand limited company must obtain an IRD number (tax file number). Where the company is incorporated through the New Zealand Companies Office and indicates a NZ income tax or GST obligation at incorporation, an IRD number is issued automatically; otherwise the company or its non-resident agent must apply via myIR or paper form IR742 (Non-Resident Company Registration), submitting the certificate of incorporation, constitution, particulars of directors and resident agent, and beneficial ownership documentation. The IRD number is generally issued within 5–10 business days. If any 12-month turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or payroll is paid, the company must simultaneously register for GST and PAYE. A foreign company carrying on business through a branch in New Zealand may also be issued an IRD number under the registered foreign-company regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a New Zealand resident limited company is taxed on its worldwide income at the corporate rate; no territorial election applies; pass-through treatment is unavailable unless a valid Look-Through Company election is made; no tax-exempt zone treatment is available within New Zealand
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Eligible close companies with 5 or fewer shareholders and no corporate shareholder may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) treatment under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007; corporate groups may elect consolidated group treatment under subpart IG; qualifying companies may elect dividend imputation credit account status; hybrid mismatch rules apply under New Zealand BEPS measures, but no US-style check-the-box election is available; a branch exemption election applies only to certain foreign attributed income under s DN 2

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 — GST registration is compulsory when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period. Non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value imported goods, including Etsy marketplace sellers and Stripe-processed supplies to New Zealand consumers, must register under the offshore-supplier GST rules when NZ-supplied goods and services exceed NZD 60,000 per annum.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transaction stamping, pre-clearance e-invoicing mandate, or digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR using forms GST-101, GST-102B, or GST-103. New Zealand has adopted the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 framework as the national e-invoicing standard, and e-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers transacting with New Zealand government agencies. Inland Revenue provides open application programming interfaces (APIs) for integrated GST return lodgement, but there is no continuous transaction control (CTC) or clearance regime requiring government pre-approval of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST-registered New Zealand supplier zero-rates exported goods under s 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the goods are exported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf within 28 days of supply. Zero-rating also applies under s 11 to services performed outside New Zealand or supplied to a non-resident for use outside New Zealand, and to deemed exports, provided the supplier holds documentary evidence of physical export or foreign use. Die-struck brass cloisonné enamel lapel pins sold through Etsy to a non-resident customer and shipped to an overseas address qualify for zero-rating, subject to production of export evidence such as carrier stamping or track-and-trace confirmation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Export Declaration / ICS Declaration)
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Receipt / bank transfer credit advice evidencing settlement in foreign currency from the non-resident purchaser
Commercial invoice with HS/ISIC classification and unit values
Carrier stamping confirmation / track-and-trace export proof from NZ Post, FedEx, DHL or other freight forwarder
Contract or purchase order evidencing overseas sale terms (EXW, FOB, CIF)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rated export claims and may re-characterise them as taxable supplies if the statutory documentary evidence bundle is incomplete or the goods or services are not in fact exported. Consequences include retrospective GST reassessment, clawback of credits and refunds already paid, shortfall penalties under s 141 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (25% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and up to 100% for evasion), use-of-money interest on unpaid or over-claimed amounts, and, in cases of serial export fraud, criminal prosecution and cancellation of GST registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) in conjunction with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA), the Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE), and the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) — Exchange control authority administered under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989 and the Overseas Investment Act 2005
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a freely floating and fully convertible currency regime on both the current account and the capital account. There are no exchange control approvals, no mandatory conversion ratios, no profit-remittance permits, and no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, branch profits, royalties, interest, or share capital to non-resident shareholders. The only statutory gateway constraints are: (i) the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which screens 'sensitive' land and 'significant business assets' transactions (inapplicable to ordinary trading of hard enamel lapel pins); and (ii) the Inland Revenue (IRD) non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) and thin capitalisation compliance for outward remittances. In practice, the de facto prior restraint on convertibility is not government control but bank-level AML/CFT and sanctions screening. Current-account transactions (export receipts from Etsy and Stripe) are wholly liberalised. Profit remittance hurdles are effectively zero for a fully compliant NZ limited company with a clean tax clearance certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand abolished all statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements, compulsory conversion timelines, and exchange-control repatriation quotas on the floating of the NZD in December 1984. A New Zealand exporter may lawfully hold 100% of its export receipts in foreign currency (USD, AUD, EUR) or convert them to NZD at any time. The only residual compliance obligations are: (i) correct recognition of export revenue in the financial statements in accordance with NZ IFRS 15; (ii) foreign-currency translation and taxation of gains/losses under the Financial Arrangements Rules (Income Tax Act 2007, subpart EW); and (iii) transaction-reporting thresholds under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (wire transfers at or above NZD 1,000 in certain circumstances).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as an auxiliary payment-settlement channel for e-commerce receipts (Etsy Direct Pay, Stripe, Shopify Payments), but MEDIUM as the sole primary operating account. Legal constraints: Offshore digital EMI providers holding only a foreign e-money licence (e.g., FCA-authorised in the UK or MAS-authorised in Singapore) are not registered banks in New Zealand under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989 and cannot take deposits in the course of carrying on business in NZ unless admitted to the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and holding a Money Services Business (MSB) registration with the Department of Internal Affairs. The Crown's 'depositor compensation scheme' protection only applies to licensed banks. To maintain tax and corporate integrity with the Inland Revenue, the Companies Office, and the FSPR, the entity should always hold at least one fallback operating account at a New Zealand-incorporated registered bank for IRD payments, company registration, and statutory-seizure compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory requirement under New Zealand law, but it remains a de facto underwriting requirement of nearly all Tier-1 banks. For an NZ-resident director, an in-branch face-to-face interview during the first onboarding stage is mandatory at ANZ, ASB, BNZ, and Westpac; Kiwibank may permit remote open for low-risk NZ entities. For a non-resident director, banks allow a fully remote or hybrid video interview (audio-video KYC) provided the director is a resident of an 'enforcement country' under the Companies Act 1993 (Australia, United Kingdom, United States, Canada, or Ireland), and can produce electronically verifiable identity documents. Directors resident in any other jurisdiction are normally required to attend a physical interview at a New Zealand branch, or alternatively at a New Zealand diplomatic post or a registered bank's correspondent overseas office with notarised attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face remote account opening where the director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a resident of a jurisdiction that is not in the 'enforcement country' list under the Companies Act 1993, and identity cannot be electronically cross-verified against NZ Companies Office or equivalent registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certified True Copies of the director's and UBO's passport bio pages; a 12-month recent original bank statement from a FATF-compliant foreign bank; an independent address verification via utility bill and land registry; a recently dated negative-media report (World-Check / Dow Jones); two professional reference letters from established counterparties including Etsy and Stripe settlement statements; a sworn affidavit of source of wealth and source of funds; and a written business plan describing the enamel-pin manufacturing and cross-border e-commerce flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (Politically Exposed Person) correlations, adverse sanctions-list hits, or previous corporate insolvency/fraud flags linked to the director or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and watchlist screening report dated no earlier than 30 days before submission; a detailed narrative of the PEP position, if any, and the source of private wealth; a certificate of good standing from the corporate registry of the foreign parent or trust; a director's declaration of no criminal convictions; and a Tier-1 bank acceptance that the account will be ring-fenced for low-value retail merchandise only, with no sovereign or state-linked counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low commercial substance in New Zealand (e.g., no real office, outsourcing all operations offshore, or use of a nominee shareholder or a bare trust in a secrecy jurisdiction).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A domestic office lease agreement or co-working membership agreement; an IRD Employer Monthly Schedule demonstrating local payroll (even part-time); purchase invoices for raw materials; the Manufacturing/Production arrangement in New Zealand or a supply-chain attestation; audited or reviewed financial statements of the ultimate parent; the full register of beneficiaries and a trust deed if a trust interposes; and a narrative of the commercial rationale for the NZ entity (e.g., 'brand provenance, Etsy marketplace seller requirements, and IRD GST registration').

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing of an inbound equity injection from a foreign shareholder requires a SWIFT MT103 wire to the entity's Capital Escrow Account at a Tier-1 New Zealand bank. The beneficiary account must be designated as 'Capital Subscription Account' and the payment details field must state: 'Share capital contribution' together with the shareholder's name and the corresponding Companies Office shareholder resolution authorising the issue or allotment of shares. Although New Zealand has no statutory purpose-code regime, banks use a de facto classification matrix: (i) code 'K' for share capital; (ii) code 'L' for shareholder loans; and (iii) code 'C' for trade/current payments. For the bank's automated monitoring, the remitter should include the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CDQC' or 'CNCB' (capital contribution). The transaction must be cross-referenced with the Companies Office share allotment filing, the IRD shareholder return, and if the parent is non-resident, the bank will typically require a board resolution and an exemption from, or acknowledgment of, non-resident withholding tax on any subsequent dividends. For amounts exceeding NZD 50,000 equivalent, the bank may ask for an evidence pack including the source of funds statement and the incorporation documents of the remitting entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the purchase of raw materials (metal blanks, cloisonné enamels, packaging) and for refunds to Etsy/Stripe buyers should be cleared via: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for all standard transactions, especially where the supplier holds a foreign bank account; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (MT700 series) for purchase orders above NZD 50,000 requiring transport documents, a certificate of origin, and a clean bill of lading; (iii) NZD domestic interbank clearings through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) for local suppliers; and (iv) the establishment of multi-currency accounts (NZD, USD, AUD, EUR) at the domestic bank to avoid double conversion of Stripe/Etsy receipts. For USD outgoing wires, the NZ bank will route through Fedwire or CHIPS via its US correspondent network. Import settlement for a NZD/USD forward contract should make use of the bank's FX conversion at the forward rate, followed by the MT103, ensuring the FX reference is included in the underlying payment instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR) with tenors from 1 week to 24 months for hedging large trade orders from Etsy/Stripe payouts
FX swaps (tomorrow-next and spot-forward combinations) to convert USD-proceeds cash flows without impacting liquidity
Cross-currency basis swaps for matching a foreign-currency receivable asset against a foreign-currency payable, where the NZ entity has both USD and AUD cash flows
Vanilla FX options (call or put on NZD, with USD, AUD, or EUR as the counter-leg) for flexible hedging of uncertain high-volume seasonal sales

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permitted in New Zealand but commercially unnecessary for the NZD, which is fully deliverable and has a liquid onshore forward market; NDFs may be used only where the underlying settlement currency belongs to a jurisdiction with exchange controls that preclude physical delivery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return confirmation of company particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: NZ Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return date is the anniversary of registration; filing is due within 28 days of that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee is imposed; failure to file triggers a breach notice and, if not remedied within 20 working days, the Registrar may strike the company off the register. On dissolution, all company assets vest in the Crown.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies unless the company qualifies as a small company under the Companies Act 1993 s199A. A small company must have total assets of NZD 3 million or less AND total revenue of NZD 6 million or less in both of the two preceding accounting periods. Exceeding either threshold in two consecutive years triggers the audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) under the XRB framework: Tier 1 and Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS; Tier 3 and Tier 4 small non-issuer companies apply the simplified reporting standards issued by the External Reporting Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate UBO annual filing exists under the Companies Act 1993. Beneficial ownership is evidenced through the shareholder and director registers. The annual return must confirm current shareholder, director, registered office, and ultimate holding company details. Share transfers recorded in the Register of Members must be reflected in the next annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable under small-company exemption; voluntary audit typically USD 5,000 - USD 15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit 15% of eligible expenditure; immediate deduction for low-value assets; non-residential building depreciation at 2% per annum; standard manufacturing expenditure deductibility; no general industry tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - New Zealand Company Income Tax Return filed via Inland Revenue myIR Secure Online Services
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March standard balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July if filed electronically through myIR, or 7 April if filed on paper; terminal tax payment due 7 February following the tax year unless covered by provisional tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income before deductions, including worldwide sales for NZ-resident companies and New Zealand-sourced income for non-resident companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies include only New Zealand-sourced income from the sale of enamel lapel pins if the sales are attributable to a New Zealand fixed establishment or permanent establishment; export sales through Etsy/Stripe to overseas customers generally are not New Zealand source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses: raw materials, contract manufacturing, dies, enamel, shipping, payment gateway fees, Etsy listing fees, and other ordinary expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if incurred in deriving assessable income; if a non-resident has a New Zealand PE, head-office overhead allocations must be arm's length and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit/(loss) before tax (Box 1 minus Box 2, adjusted for non-deductible items).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with no PE cannot offset losses against New Zealand income; any loss claimed must satisfy the shareholder continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account and dividend information, including any shareholder dividend distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must have Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) deducted at the applicable statutory or treaty rate; imputation credits are not refundable to non-residents unless a DTA expressly allows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by a director or authorised officer that the return is true and correct.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no director is resident in New Zealand, a New Zealand resident agent with a valid IRD number and signed authority must file and declare the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250, incremental penalties of NZD 250 per month up to NZD 2,500, late payment penalties of 1% on day 1 and 4% by day 7 plus 1% per month thereafter, and shortfall penalties for incorrect returns of 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall depending on culpability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; reduced under DTAs to 15% for portfolio shareholdings and commonly 5% for substantial direct shareholdings (e.g. 10% or 25% voting ownership).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must deliver to the New Zealand company an IRD declaration form (IR67 or equivalent) affirming residence and eligibility for a reduced NRWT rate, together with an original or certified Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty-country revenue authority. The certificate must be valid for the period in which the dividend is paid, and the shareholder must not have a New Zealand permanent establishment to which the dividend is attributable. The NZ payer is entitled to withhold at the treaty rate only once the declaration and TRC are held before payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties paid to non-residents is 15% of gross royalties; DTAs often reduce to 10% or 5%. Statutory NRWT on interest is 15% of gross interest, with treaty rates commonly 0% to 10%; NZ borrowers may elect the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% on interest paid to unassociated non-resident lenders on qualifying registered securities, in lieu of NRWT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions triggers the expectation of contemporaneous Local File-style transfer pricing documentation; multinational groups with New Zealand operations and consolidated global revenue exceeding EUR 750 million (approximately NZD 1.3 billion) must additionally prepare Master File and Country-by-Country Report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have separate Economic Substance Regulations as in offshore financial centres, but substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1), the voidable arrangement provisions (s GB 1), thin capitalisation rules, non-resident controlled company rules, and the requirement that any tax-residency, transfer-pricing, or head-office cost-allocation claim be supported by actual decision-making, employees, premises, contracts, and commercial rationale in New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting revenue from Etsy/Stripe sales, fabricating purchase invoices, destroying sales records, or dishonestly understating taxable profits of the New Zealand company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Conviction under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A or s 143B may attract a fine up to NZD 50,000 for first offence and up to NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, plus imprisonment for a term up to 5 years; the company may also be ordered to pay the full tax shortfall plus shortfall penalties up to 150%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally participated in or directed the evasion may be prosecuted as parties to the offence, face the same fines and imprisonment, and may be barred from managing a company under the Companies Act 1993; civil restitution of diverted corporate funds may also be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the New Zealand limited company with no real commercial activity, no New Zealand bank account or physical presence, no active director oversight, and using the entity solely to hold intellectual property or route Etsy sales while distributing all profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar of Companies may initiate compulsory strike-off under the Companies Act 1993, deregister the entity, and forfeit its assets to the Crown; the company's income may be recharacterised by Inland Revenue as derived by a shadow associate or the controller, with penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for debts and tax if they allow the company to trade while insolvent, fail to keep proper accounting records, or permit the company to be used to defeat tax; the High Court may impose a management ban of up to 10 years and order compensation for creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 when the business in fact provides services caught by the Act, or deliberately concealing beneficial ownership and source-of-funds information despite receiving suspicious transfers from overseas enamel-pin buyers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Austrac-style penalties are not applicable; under the AML/CFT Act 2009, non-compliance with due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or prescribed transaction reports may attract civil fines of up to NZD 200,000 for individuals and NZD 2 million for companies per contravention, plus criminal sanctions for knowingly false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors can be personally fined and may face criminal liability for willful non-compliance; a director who facilitates money laundering through the company's accounts commits an offence under the Crimes Act 1961 and may be imprisoned for up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated fees to an associated Hong Kong or Singapore shell supplier for enamel pin manufacturing, or artificially reducing NZ taxable profits through excessive royalties, management fees, or intercompany interest without arm's-length benchmarking or contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may adjust the taxable income to an arm's-length amount under Income Tax Act 2007 ss GC 13-GC 15, impose a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall, and apply late payment interest; the tax shortfall itself remains payable without restructure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or knowingly allow uncommercial related party pricing may incur personal liability for penalties, and if the arrangement is found to be tax avoidance, the anti-avoidance provisions can reach the controlling shareholder personally, including piercing the corporate veil for restitution, asset freezing orders, and travel bans pending criminal investigation.
